Noah floated grandly above THE Wastes, the multicolored rain continuing to fall around him as if the Existence itself was weeping for what had been declared!

He saw himself represented in that golden box.

He saw eighty-one other golden boxes bearing the names of his family and those who followed him.

His mother. His son. His lovers. His companions. His allies. Even his penguin!

All chosen to be pitted against Primordial Architects and monsters of THE Second Scale.

They wanted to butcher his people without him even being able to help them.

Each battle would occur in isolated arenas where he couldnt intervene. Each confrontation would pit someone he loved against beings who had existed for eons, who had forged Proterozoic Bones and Organs across spans that made human lifetimes seem like heartbeats.

He had only ever defended himself.

He had never asked for anything grand. He had never wanted anything grand. His dreams were simple. Safety. Prosperity. Happiness. A plot of land and seas of Mana!

But he would always be targeted.

This was why he never stood still. This was why he continued to seek and to dream. This was why he pushed himself past limitations that others said couldnt be surpassed!

Because of shit like this.

Because the moment he stopped growing, the moment he accepted contentment, the moment he believed he had finally achieved enough, something like this would descend upon him and everyone he cared about.

THE Deliverance had declared war.

Not against him directly, where his Hadean body could meet whatever was thrown at it. Against his people. Against those whose only crime was being connected to his Civilization through bonds of loyalty and love.

Twenty-four hours.

He had twenty-four hours before his mother faced a Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect alone.

Before everyone he cared about was thrown into battles they were never meant to survive.

Noahs eyes blazed like singularities of cold fury as he looked upon the declaration still burning in the sky above THE Wastes!

Chapter 5112: I Volunteer!

If one wasnt loud in existence, others might think they were meek and could get pushed around.

Noah didnt like to be loud. He preferred results that spoke louder than words ever could. But he could be very loud if he wanted. He could shake the foundations of Observable Existence itself if the situation demanded it!

Now they wanted to target him and his family?

To isolate his mother, his son, and everyone else he cared about in domains with Calymmian Proterozoic Scale entities in less than 24 hours?

Okay.

This was a deadly and terrifying move on their behalf. THE Deliverance had called upon THE First Cause itself to enforce this Civilizational Holy War, with matchups designed to slaughter everyone connected to his Civilization while he watched helplessly from outside their isolated arenas.

But they made one critical mistake.

That mistake was giving him 24 hours.

Others experienced major changes across thousands or millions of years. They cultivated Proterozoic Bones one at a time over spans that most beings couldnt comprehend. They refined their Organs through patient accumulation that treated centuries like days.

He could flip the whole fucking board in a matter of hours.

He had done it before. He would do it again.

Noah glared at the golden and platinum boxes still burning in the sky above THE Wastes, his mind already racing through possibilities and contingencies. He was preparing to leave when an instant later, a voice reached him.

"When adversity comes, it doesnt end, it seems."

THE Primordial Paradoxs words held the weight of someone who had observed eons of conflict and understood exactly what was at stake.

"I received weavings of existence explaining the Civilizational Holy War and my potential position within it. Tell me whose slot among your people you need me to take, Youngest. I will be there for you."

Before Noah could respond, another voice reached him at nearly the same moment. Alexanders words overlapped with those of THE Great Usurper, both of them arriving simultaneously as if existence itself was ensuring he understood that he wasnt alone.

"The fallout from that fight still seems to be cascading. Im sorry about this. Tell me whose position to take."

Alexanders voice carried guilt!

"Osmont!"

THE Great Usurpers voice boomed with energy.

"While we may be getting curbstomped since I havent gotten too far yet, Im also here to help however you need me to. Just say the word. I have uh...made friends with Abaddon and the many Chaos Giants of Jotunheim among other things. Being idle and active at the same time is paying off. ."

...!

They reached out to him one after another, making it clear they would help. They only asked him how.

Amser Modreds voice arrived around the same time, THE Living Temporals words burning with time!

"My Civilizational Anchor has just been established. I can use the test against monstrous beings and my weavings of Time. Let me know."

...!

Noahs eyes flashed sharply as he processed all of these offers.

He sent each of them their own replies, his thoughts pressing outward through connections that had been established across various circumstances and conflicts. The message was the same for all of them: hang on for now, and he would let them know something soon enough.

He was about to move when another message arrived.

This one came differently. Not through direct communication or Civilizational weavings, but through slivers of tumultuous emotions gathered from all across existence.

A voice from a woman he really didnt like hearing from. Even more than the voice, something physical manifested before his perception.

The multicolored rain falling throughout THE Wastes began behaving strangely.

Droplets paused in their descent. Others curved toward a central point. Emotions that permeated the very fabric of this transformed region, residual feelings left over from the conflict that had occurred here, began coalescing into something visible.

An illusory visage formed from the gathered emotional resonance!

THE Living Emotive looked toward Noah with shining eyes that held something far beyond normal attention. Her features were beautiful in a way that felt dangerous...symmetry that seemed designed to draw others in before consuming them!

Her smile stretched too wide. Her gaze never quite settled, flickering between points of focus as if she was perceiving things that existed only in her own unstable perception.

Her voice reached out through the illusory phenomena with mania that made his skin crawl.

"Sir Osmont!"

The words tumbled out rapidly, barely controlled.

"I volunteer! I volunteer as tribute! How dare these decrepit Primordial Architects try to bully you?! The audacity! The sheer presumption! They think they can threaten whats yours? Whats MINE to protect?!"

Her illusory form flickered, features shifting between expressions faster than should have been possible.

"I have tapped into all emotions across Observable Existence! Every feeling! Every passion! Every rage and love and despair! They flow through me like rivers through valleys, and I will use them ALL for you!"

She giggled, the sound carrying eerie undertones that Noah didnt want to examine too closely.

"I will focus on penetrating into THE Wyld! I sense THE Creature has arrived there, and where he goes, interesting things follow...I will gather information for you of the Civilizations and power of those trying to bully you!"

Her eyes locked onto his with intensity that bordered on religious fervor.

"I dont want anything in return. Just keep me in your thoughts! I know you detest me... I know you may even want to kill me, but I...really want you! Like... ah!"

She shuddered visibly, the illusory form rippling with emotional overflow.

"Ill get back to you as I have to focus to penetrate weavings of THE Wyld! Think of me, Osmont! Think of me! Think of me!"

The visage faded, emotions dispersing back into the surrounding environment as quickly as they had gathered.

...!

What... the fuck?

Noahs eyes turned sharp as he processed what had just occurred. Had that woman gotten so powerful after claiming Chaos?

He didnt even want to bother with that right now!

Moments after her departure, his weavings buzzed again as another voice arrived. This one came from someone he actually respected.

Anaximanders words echoed out.

"Hey, big guy."

The greeting was simple.

"The other big guy Im moving with in THE Wyld right now will probably tell me not to interfere. Hell say you need to handle your adversity yourself, that challenges only make you stronger, all that philosophical stuff hes fond of."

A slight pause came that felt almost apologetic.

"But THE Deliverance is nasty stuff. Real nasty. So just like before, just say Come, Anaximander! and I will be there."

...!

Chapter 5113: Custodes! I

The voice of Anaximander echoed through his mind as Noah turned silent.

He was moving with THE Creature within THE Wyld right now. Among all those who had reached out to offer assistance, THE Creature was notably not among them.

Noah knew the beings philosophy. Adversity only made one stronger. Pain was the forge that shaped greatness. THE Creature wouldnt volunteer himself because doing so would undermine the very principles he had built his existence around. He believed Noah needed to face this challenge.

But Noah also knew that if he asked, this being who had burned away his own Primordial Architect classification would come.

But did he truly need to do so?

This was not THE Fable of THE Creature. This wasnt someone elses story where Noah played a supporting role, benefiting from anothers power while his own remained stagnant.

This was his life. His weavings. His story.

And he would do everything he could to depend on himself and the weavings of his existence.

At this moment in time, there were several things he wanted to do. The first relied on himself, yes, but also drew from a place he was already pulling significant power from. A being whose Observable Force flooded into him constantly.

He wouldnt ask for help from her either.

But with his Hadean weavings, he was about to do many crazy things that would pull even more from her reserves. He wanted to talk with her before then. To give her a heads up, and to also make sure that in addition to THE Deliverance, he wouldnt add Gilded Lifeforms as his enemies right now. So he would reach out towards her.

Toward the one who was supposedly so far from him.

Toward Ubergulden Adelheid.

"Ruination," he said. "Set up the line of communication between me and Ubergulden Adelheid. Wherever she may be."

...!

|Understood, Master.|

Ruinations voice emerged, already working on his request.

|Communication with Ubergulden Adelheid presents unique challenges due to the nature of your connection and the distances involved. However, your Hadean transformation has expanded the capabilities available through your bond.|

|Initiating communication protocol.|

|The seas of Observable Force connecting you to Ubergulden Adelheid serve as the primary conduit. Information can travel along the same pathways that authority travels. Your Quintessence Infiniforce resides within Ubergulden Adelheid heavily.|

|Establishing resonance between your Hadean existence and the Observable Force conduit. Establishing resonance between your Quintessence Infiniforce within Ubergulden Adelheid and your primary reserves.|

|Communication channel established.|

|You may now speak directly to Ubergulden Adelheid through this connection. Your words will reach her regardless of physical distance. Her responses will return through the same pathways.|

|Speak, and she will hear.|

...!

Noah took a breath that his Hadean lungs didnt technically require.

Then he reached out through the connection!

---

<Unknown Region of Existence>

She loved the triumph of the weak.

There was something beautiful about it, something that stirred feelings Ubergulden Adelheid had never been able to fully explain to others of her kind. When something small and fragile rose against something vast and terrible, when it struggled and bled and somehow emerged victorious despite every factor working against it, she felt something close to hope.

But such triumphs were always short-lived.

They never produced long-lasting results. The weak could win a battle, could celebrate their moment of glory, could believe they had changed the fundamental nature of their circumstances. Then reality would reassert itself, and everything they had fought for would crumble back into the dust it had always been destined to become.

She was currently standing inside a vast room that defied normal spatial comprehension.

The walls seemed to breathe with golden light, surfaces that werent quite solid shifting through configurations of architecture built from principles most civilizations couldnt perceive.

Constellations drifted across the ceiling in patterns that held meaning only to those engineered to read them as they depicted the emergence of...Causes.

The floor beneath her feet felt like standing on crystallized purpose, every step resonating with power refined across spans that predated THE First Cause.

This was a glimpse of what truly advanced Civilizations looked like when they had access to resources that Bounded could never touch.

This was how THE Gilded lived.

Throughout the room, figures stood at various positions with postures of attentive service. Their skin shone with golden coloring that declared their nature without need for introduction, each one radiating authority that would have made someone like Grimvault feel like absolutely nothing.

The aura these servants held felt hundreds of times grander than what that Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect could muster at his peak.

Yet their faces held only respect when they looked toward her.

THE Gesinde. The lowest classification of Gilded Lifeforms, those who served at the pleasure of unique and grander Gilded. Even the weakest among them could have crushed basic Primordial Architects with casual effort, could have unmade Civilizations that Bounded considered unbreakable.

They were servants only in relation to beings like herself, and that relationship gave a glimpse to hierarchies that most of Observable Existence couldnt comprehend.

Ubergulden Adelheid was seated on a floating golden lotus, its petals radiating warmth that nourished her existence simply through contact. Before her floated a golden aquarium filled with waters that shifted between blue and luminescent gold, containing a landscape of coral formations and underwater valleys that stretched for what appeared to be mere feet but actually encompassed light years of compressed space.

She was watching a group of goldfish.

These werent ordinary creatures. Each one burned with power at the Fundamental Depth of THE First Scale, their small forms containing authority that would have made them legendary figures in most regions of Observable Existence. The concentration of existence and Observable Force was so potent here that even simple lifeforms naturally attained the peak of THE First Scale through mere proximity to Gilded environments.

The water around them swirled with blue-gold blood, their scales torn and fins shredded from recent combat. But they were celebrating, swimming in patterns that declared triumph despite their injuries. They had just defended their territory against a threat that should have been impossible for them to overcome.

A golden crab floated listlessly ahead of them, its massive form drifting with the current.

It had been at THE Absolute Depth of THE First Scale. It had threatened their home, had invaded their small corner of this aquarium with intent to consume everything they had built. And they had fought back. They had coordinated, had sacrificed, had pushed themselves past limitations that should have been absolute.

They had won!

Ubergulden Adelheid watched them celebrate with eyes that held something close to sorrow.

Because what the goldfish couldnt see was what existed on the other side of this aquarium. Beyond the coral formations and underwater valleys, past the territories they considered their entire world, thousands of those crabs clustered in configurations that of organized society rather than mindless predation. They had just sensed one of their own be killed.

They were already sending a party.

These goldfish that had triumphed against their oppressor, that were currently swimming in patterns of joy and relief, would all find themselves dead soon enough. The weak had won a battle. The weak would lose the war. As they always did. As they always would.

The weak never won. Not truly.

They only delayed their deaths.

Chapter 5114: Custodes! II

As she was thinking all this, lost in contemplation that had consumed her attention across eons of observation, a voice reached her through pathways that shouldnt have been accessible.

"Hey."

The greeting was nonchalant and natural, almost familiar in its casualness. She found herself nodding and responding lightly before her conscious mind caught up with what was happening.

"Hey."

Then her eyes opened wide.

Across the room, THE Gesinde turned toward her with expressions of mild confusion. They blinked as if trying to determine who she was talking to, their perception scanning the space around her for the source of a conversation they couldnt perceive. Did she call for them?

Ubergulden Adelheid controlled her expression with discipline cultivated across countless eons.

Internally, she was shocked. She reached into her existence, following the pathways through which that greeting had traveled, and found its origin in the endless Quintessence Infiniforce integrated throughout her being. The voice had been Osmonts!

It had traveled through the connection between them!

But this...shouldnt have been possible.

How did he reach through unreachable weavings to be capable of sending even a communication? The connection established was one-directional. Information, communication, anything else should have been blocked by countermeasures she had implemented specifically to prevent exactly this scenario!

She focused on the Quintessence Infiniforce saturating her existence.

And shockingly, she began to see something forming within those multicolored seas. An illusory outline took shape, features becoming distinct as her perception refined its focus. It was Osmont, his form constructed from the very Infinity he had integrated into her being, manifesting in a space that existed entirely within her own existence.

Her expression grew heavier.

Part of her own weavings coalesced internally, her consciousness shifting to engage with this intrusion directly. Inside her body. In an expanse of multicolored Quintessence Infiniforce swirling all around.

Noahs illusory visage finished forming.

From his perspective, all he could see were these endless multicolored seas stretching in every direction. Golden walls blocked off absolutely everything past the areas where these seas were contained, barriers she had constructed to prevent exactly this kind of penetration. He couldnt sense or see a thing beyond the Infiniforce that belonged to him.

Good.

Moments later, a very real and very angry Ubergulden Adelheid appeared within these seas.

She looked at him with an imperious gaze that held fury barely restrained beneath its surface. Her golden eyes blazed as she spoke with authority that pressed against his illusory form.

"I was magnanimous enough to leave you be, but you do this? You give a Bounded a mile, they reach for light years..."

Her voice cut through the swirling Infiniforce like a blade.

"What do you want? Are you unable to take care of the entanglements you have gotten yourself into down there? Are you running to me for help now?"

She stepped closer to his illusory form, her presence overwhelming despite existing only as a projection within her own internal space.

"I.. cannot help you."

She berated him with everything she had because he truly didnt understand what she had already done for him. The less he was connected to her, the more he wouldnt be found out. Because if he was found out by those who mattered, he would be killed.

Killed, erased so thoroughly that even the concept of his existence would be scrubbed from Observable Existence as if he had never been.

She had done what she could to preserve his life.

And he was doing this now?

She gazed toward him with calm anger burning in her golden eyes as he blinked calmly, his expression unchanged by her fury.

"I can take care of my own things."

His voice was steady and almost amused.

"I just reached out to check in on you and to notify you of a few things I have planned. I just didnt expect you to be so charged up, O Great Gilded One."

The last part came out almost mockingly, and Ubergulden Adelheids eyes became sharp.

"You did all this to check in on me?"

Noah nodded as he looked around at the golden walls and swirling Infiniforce surrounding them.

"You left the weavings of Gilded Lifeforms eons ago to live as a Bounded, so it must have sucked. Youre now back where you ran away from."

His eyes returned to hers.

"How does it feel?"

...!

How did it feel?

Ubergulden Adelheid blinked as she found herself without words. She didnt even know how to reply to such a question. She alone knew why she had left here and suppressed herself to live as a Bounded Lifeform. She alone knew the circumstances that had driven her to abandon everything her engineering had granted her. And she alone knew how she felt now that she had returned.

But this was something she had never shared with anyone.

She wouldnt start now.

She regained her imperious bearing with effort that didnt show on her face. Her gaze traveled over Osmonts illusory form, examining it with perception that could see things his classification shouldnt have been able to hide.

Her eyes flashed sharply.

"You seem to have changed and advanced somewhat. Are you enjoying the little connection and siphoning youve been taking from me?"

Noah looked at his arms, examining them with interest as if noticing his own transformation for the first time.

"Thats what I was actually going to mention to you. I dont know much about Gilded Lifeforms, but in the near future, Ill likely be widening and further fortifying our connection."

He looked back up at her.

"I just wanted to make sure a little, tiny Bounded ant like me wont cause any problems for you and your reserves of existence. And I also dont wish to expose myself for being too loud so...fortify yourself to make sure nothing leaks."

...!

Ubergulden Adelheid raised her brows at this before shaking her head.

"You wont be able to do much. The connection we have stops at that. Ive made sure of it, and even if I do nothing, a Bounded cannot alter or change much when it comes to the state of a Gilded."

Her voice carried certainty born from understanding.

"Even if I didnt already set up countermeasures. If you wish to fully remove any risk from yourself, you can always pull back your weavings of Infinity from me."

...!

After she said these words, Noah nodded slowly.

"I just wanted to pass on the message so that youre not too surprised. Going back to a place you ran away from for eons can be disorienting, so I hope you are adjusting well."

His illusory form began to flicker at the edges.

"If you need to talk, just reach out to Infinity. Im also very curious about you and all things to do with Ubergulden Adelheid. Ill be dealing with a Civilizational Holy War for now but Ill check in as things progress. Hang in there, O Big and Great Gilded One."

...!

Ubergulden Adelheids eyes opened wide at hearing her true name spoken from his mouth, and then ending his words mockingly again!

How did he find out her identity? The countermeasures she had implemented should have prevented anyone from perceiving what she truly was.

She was going to ask.

But the moment his words finished, his illusory form dispersed and fell back into the roiling Quintessence Infiniforce. He had dropped such a bomb and left immediately after, knowing she would want to reach out to him now, knowing she would have questions that demanded answers.

Ubergulden Adelheids eyes shone sharply.

She would never reach out to him. She was going to grasp the Containment she had placed on the Quintessence Infiniforce in her body, was going to reinforce the barriers that should have prevented this communication from ever occurring in the first place.

But at this moment, a voice echoed through the vast room.

"Sister, it is time."

...!

The voice of Ubergulden Dietrich filled the space as THE Gesinde throughout the room stood at attention with perfect synchronization.

A door opened in one of those breathing golden walls, revealing her brothers unfathomably handsome features and the golden eyes that held no pupils.

Behind him stood a few more Gilded Lifeforms!

Chapter 5115: Custodes! III

Ubergulden Dietrich stepped through the doorway with the easy confidence of someone who had never known limitation.

Behind him walked three women draped in golden robes that seemed woven from solidified gold Infinity. Their features held the ageless beauty common to all Gilded, but something about their bearing suggested wisdom accumulated across spans that made even other Gilded seem young.

Each one radiated authority that pressed against the room in waves of measured power.

The Magna Sorora.

Ubergulden Adelheid recognized them immediately. This grand sisterhood existed solely to ensure the primacy and progression of Gilded Ones, their membership consisting entirely of wise women who had dedicated their existences to guiding their kind toward greater heights. They advised ruling families, oversaw ceremonies of significance, and maintained traditions that predated most of what currently existed in Observable Existence.

The first among them was called Sororis Prima Evangelina, her features sharp and assessing beneath hair that fell like spun gold. The second, Sororis Prima Konstanze, held herself with the stillness of deep water concealing dangerous currents. The third, Sororis Prima Mathilde, watched everything with eyes that seemed to perceive far more than they revealed.

All three studied Ubergulden Adelheid with attention that felt like physical pressure.

"Sister."

Ubergulden Dietrichs voice carried warmth beneath its formal cadence as he approached her floating lotus.

"They are here for the preliminary process before you can be taken to the ceremony. Today marks your full rejoining with all the status your position in our ruling family demands."

He smiled.

"This means one of the first things in your Ceremony is for you to undergo the Bonding, THE Sundesmos, with your own Custodes."

Custodes.

The word stirred memories that Ubergulden Adelheid had suppressed across eons of living as someone else. A Custos, in singular form, was a powerful Gilded One bound to ruling royal Gilded through rituals.

They protected their bonded charge for life, their existences intertwined so thoroughly that betrayal became impossible by design. Should anything threaten their bonded Gilded One, the Custodes would pay with their lives before allowing harm to reach those they served.

They were unfathomably loyal because they were engineered to be incapable of anything else.

"The one chosen to be your Custos is someone who grew up and trained with us," Dietrich continued, his golden eyes without pupils brightening with something like nostalgia. "You remember Wachter Alaric, yes? He has been preparing for this responsibility since you departed. His dedication to your eventual return has been quite touching, actually."

Ubergulden Adelheid remained calm.

She had known this was coming when she agreed to return. She had understood what playing the role she had run away from would require. The ceremonies, the obligations, the chains disguised as honors that would bind her to a life she had abandoned precisely because it suffocated everything she actually wanted to be.

"Let us just get this process started."

Her voice carried none of the turmoil that existed beneath her composed exterior. She had fully come back and committed to this path. Whatever personal feelings she held about Bonding, about Custodes, about becoming once again what her family demanded, those feelings were irrelevant now.

She had made her choice.

The three Sororis Prima moved forward with synchronized grace, their golden robes trailing across the floor like liquid infinity. They circled her floating lotus with slow deliberate steps, their eyes never leaving her form as they completed one rotation, then another.

"The preliminary testing will now commence," Sororis Prima Evangelina announced, her voice carrying the weight of ritual. "Ubergulden Adelheid, daughter of one of the noble lines, you will remain still while we verify your readiness for the Bonding ceremony."

Illusory golden blades materialized in their hands.

The weapons shimmered with authority that could have unmade lesser beings through proximity alone. Each Sororis Prima raised her blade as they continued circling, the ritual taking form through movements practiced across countless ceremonies before this one.

Then, as one, they struck.

Three golden blades pierced the neck of Ubergulden Adelheid from different angles, passing through flesh that offered no resistance because the weapons werent meant to harm. They were meant to read. To perceive what existed within her on levels that normal examination couldnt access.

Ubergulden Adelheid didnt react.

She gazed on calmly and waited, her expression unchanged as the illusory blades remained embedded in her neck. This was standard procedure. This was what returning to her position required. She had known they would examine her, would verify that eons of living as Bounded hadnt corrupted her engineering in ways that made the Bonding impossible.

She had covered everything with her power to make sure nothing would be found out.

But...

The calm expressions of the Magna Sorora began to shift.

Sororis Prima Evangelinas brow furrowed slightly. Sororis Prima Konstanzes stillness became rigid rather than relaxed. Sororis Prima Mathildes eyes widened by a fraction that most beings wouldnt have noticed.

Confusion spread across their features.

Then shock.

Then anger.

They pulled back from Ubergulden Adelheid with sudden movements that shattered the rituals measured grace. Their golden blades dissolved as they retreated, their expressions now holding coldness that pressed against the room with force that made THE Gesinde throughout the space lower their heads instinctively as they kneeled!

"She is already bound to a Custos!"

BOOM!

Sororis Prima Evangelinas voice cut through the silence like a blade far sharper than the illusory ones she had wielded.

"She has undergone the Sundesmos ritual!"

...!

The words fell into the room and detonated.

Ubergulden Dietrichs expression transformed from warm anticipation to cold shock in the span of a single heartbeat. His golden eyes without pupils fixed on his sister with intensity that could have crushed thousands of Folds through attention alone!

The anger that followed came fast, displacing the shock before it had fully settled.

"You..."

His voice emerged low.

"Who did you bind to? What have you done?!"

He stepped toward her, his presence expanding with fury that made the three Sororis Prima retreat further despite their own considerable power because he knew where she had been thks whole time.

She had not been around Gilded so who could she have possibly become bound to? He already knew the answer as it was obscene!

"Do you not know your position?! How you need someone strong to help you for what is coming?! Otherwise you wont survive!"

His hands clenched at his sides, golden light bleeding between his fingers.

"Tell me, who... who is your Custos?"

...!

Ubergulden Adelheids shock didnt show on her face, but it cascaded through her existence!

She hadnt undergone the Sundesmos ritual.

She hadnt bound herself to any Custos.

She had lived as Bounded for eons, had suppressed her engineering, had existed without any of the connections that defined Gilded hierarchy. The Bonding ceremony today was supposed to be her first. There was no one. There couldnt be anyone?

"..."

Motherfucker.

She placed her hand on her heart.

And she sensed the boundless Quintessence Infiniforce swirling within her, multicolored seas that belonged to someone who had somehow reached through unreachable weavings to communicate with her mere moments ago.

Fuck!

She stayed silent.

Because she didnt know how to explain that her Custos, the Custodes she had bound...might be a Bounded Lifeform she had never actually chosen to bind herself to at all!

She could not explain this!

Chapter 5116: THE First Infinite Scale! I

As he utilized that connection to converse with Eon, or really, Ubergulden Adelheid, Noah hadnt been sitting still.

There was something he had already been doing with another body as he received the declaration of the Civilizational Holy War from THE Deliverance. While one body had been focusing on the mass transformation of many of his people to become Nascent Hadean Lifeforms, another body had been giving specialized care to none other than Naldine Manthon.

She was a unique one due to her power.

He wanted to gauge exactly what Hadean would mean for someone at THE Second Scale, someone who had already established their Civilizational Anchor and wielded authority that most beings couldnt comprehend. He also wanted to confirm his own capabilities in an area that made progression slightly more fun, an area that combined multiple hobbies he had cultivated across his journey.

The result was exemplary.

At this moment, Noahs body was draped in a loose robe as he sat atop a flat grassland on a floating landmass. This small island was the only territory for light years in every direction, with radiant blue seas stretching endlessly around him. The waters churned with gentle currents that carried infinity in concentrations that would have overwhelmed most beings.

This realm had taken the qualities of Oceanus.

But the most striking feature wasnt the sea around them. It was the sky above. A few miles high, what should have been atmosphere was actually another sea that stretched out endlessly, its waters suspended through principles that defied physics. Looking up meant looking into depths rather than heights, waves rolling across an inverted ocean that reflected the one below.

He was within a small island in such a place within THE Infiniverse.

The only other being present was adjusting her breathing while radiating terrifying power.

Naldine Manthon sat several meters away from him, her radiant white hair slightly messy from recent exertion. A white robe draped over her body in ways that suggested it had been hastily arranged. Her singularity-dotted eyes held something between disbelief and wonder as she examined her own existence.

Every single bone in her body pulsed with light.

Every single organ blazed with authority that pressed against the surrounding environment.

All of them had become Proterozoic through the process Noah had guided her through. This was the result of transforming her into a Nascent Hadean Lifeform while also carrying out their first session of Dual Cultivation, the combination of methodologies producing effects that exceeded what either would have achieved alone!

The golden crack on her forehead, that marking of Nascent Hadean classification, seemed to glow brighter than what he had observed on Barbatos or the others. Her white hair now held rivers of gold Observable Force threading through it like veins of precious metal through marble.

At this time, Naldine Manthon dripped with power dozens of times grander than her old self.

She raised her hand before her face, watching the light pulse through flesh that had been fundamentally altered. Her glistening bones became visible beneath her skin for a moment, crystalline structures that declared their Proterozoic nature without need for deeper examination. She shook her head as if she didnt want to believe what she was perceiving.

Noah looked at her from the corner of his eyes.

Then he looked at the prompts detailing her changes.

|Focus options for Hadean Infinity of Development include but are not limited to: Civilization advancement and refinement, study and usage of Pulses, physical capability enhancement, perception expansion, or any other relevant aspect of her existence she wishes to prioritize.|

...!

The results with Naldine were astounding.

Even she didnt seem to believe it. She continued examining her hand, watching the light pulse through bones that had been ordinary by Primordial Architect standards mere hours ago.

She shook her head slowly.

"Fuck."

Noah looked over and blinked at the single word that emerged from her mouth. His expression shifted to something that might have been innocent confusion if one didnt know him better.

"I thought you wanted to rest a bit, but okay."

...!

He said such words as if he were an unwilling participant being asked to resume activities he had only begrudgingly engaged in!

As if the Dual Cultivation had been entirely her idea and he was simply accommodating her requests out of politeness.

Naldine looked toward him with cold eyes that held dangerous promise.

"You stay back. Youve done enough!"

Her voice carried authority that pressed against the island they occupied, waves in the surrounding seas responding to her displeasure by churning more violently.

"I need to gauge myself first to make sure you have not infused me with THE Gamaidjan..."

She looked at her other hand, then back to him with suspicion.

"This much Infinity swirling in ones existence... how can you possibly not go mad? Is your Infinity different than the Infinity the rest of us know and use?"

Chapter 5117: THE First Infinite Scale! II

Was his Infinity different compared to others?

Who could say. He had touched Infinity when he was nothing but a human throwing fireballs. He had integrated it so thoroughly into his existence that separation seemed impossible now. Perhaps the very act of claiming it so early, before he understood what he was grasping, had changed both him and what Infinity meant within his existence.

Noah rose up and stretched, his loose robe shifting around a body that blazed with Hadean authority.

"After cycling through my existence, maybe I tame the Infinity you all know entirely and make it something else. Maybe thats why I can fill myself and others with it, and no madness comes."

He looked toward Naldine with eyes that shone like singularities.

"But forget that. Use your Hadean Infinity of Development. See if you can rapidly transform your Proterozoic Bones to Hadean Bones."

...!

He was initially going to ask her what she knew about going from Calymmian to Ediacaran. That knowledge could have been valuable, would have given him insight into how Primordial Architects structured their progression through the tiers of THE Second Scale.

But he didnt want to be influenced too much on his own progression.

He was choosing to go in a direction that was entirely his own. Vakochevs Scales had served as a useful framework for understanding where others stood, but they werent his framework. They werent designed to account for what he was becoming. They werent built to measure someone who held Hadean classification while still technically at THE First Scale.

What he wanted to do now was complex and simple all at once.

"Ruination, let me see an outline of the ninth potential First Infinite Scale progression weve designed."

...!

Yes.

He had actually made blueprints of nine potential systems of progression and tweaked things as he went. Each iteration refined the concepts, eliminated redundancies, and brought him closer to something that felt right. He wanted to stop at the ninth one because otherwise he felt like he would have continued going until the eighty-first potential system design, and that much deliberation would have consumed time he didnt have.

The declaration of Civilizational Holy War pressed against the back of his mind. Twenty-four hours. Less now. Every moment spent designing was a moment not spent preparing his people for what was coming!

But this design would determine everything that followed.

|Displaying the ninth iteration of THE First Infinite Scale of Existence.|

Ruinations voice emerged as golden light coalesced before him, forming diagrams and notations that outlined his vision.

|You have structured your First Infinite Scale into three major demarcations, each representing a distinct phase of development before officially stepping toward what you will design later as THE Second Infinite Scale.|

|The foundational pillars of this progression are Infinity through Quintessence Infiniforce, Observable Force, and Civilizations as actualized building blocks through THE First Tongue.|

|First Demarcation: Infinitas Corpus, The Infinite Body.|

|This is where you currently stand at the peak. Your entire skeletal structure and organ systems have achieved Hadean classification. Your grasp of Infinity exists at the level of Uncountable Infinity, which saturates every aspect of your being without limit or boundary.|

|The requirements for completing this demarcation are: Full Hadean transformation of all 206 bones and 78 organs, stable integration of Uncountable Infinity throughout existence, and the capacity to channel both Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force simultaneously without conflict.|

|You have fulfilled all requirements. The First Demarcation is complete.|

|Second Demarcation: Infinitas Architectura, The Infinite Architecture.|

|This phase focuses on the construction of a singular internal structure that will serve as the foundation for everything that follows. You will build a Hadean Pillar of Infinity within your existence.|

|This single Pillar differs from conventional cultivation foundations in a critical way. Rather than constructing multiple separate pillars for different authorities, you will construct one Pillar that can be built up by as many Civilizations as you can actualize within it.|

|Through THE First Tongue, you can currently access and embody any Civilization temporarily. Infinitas Architectura requires you to move beyond temporary access toward permanent actualization. Each Civilization you congeal into stable form becomes another layer of your Hadean Pillar of Infinity, another foundation stone supporting the structure you are building.|

|There is no upper limit to how many Civilizations can be integrated into your Hadean Pillar. The more Civilizations you actualize within it, the grander and more stable the Pillar becomes. Observable Force serves as the binding agent holding these actualized Civilizations together. Quintessence Infiniforce serves as the animating principle that allows them to function as a unified whole rather than separate fragments.|

|THE Infiniverse can contribute to this process. Her own Hadean transformation provides templates for how internal structures can be organized. As her backbone becomes Hadean, resonance between your existences will accelerate the construction of your Pillar.|

|To complete this demarcation and progress to the third, you must achieve Absolute Infinity. This represents Infinity that has transcended mere uncountability to become self-referential and complete. Absolute Infinity can observe itself, can contain itself, can become both the container and the contained...well, potentially, we still dont know. Only when your grasp of Infinity reaches this level will the transition to your third demarcation become possible.|

|Third Demarcation: Infinitas Causa, The Infinite Cause.|

|This is the final phase of THE First Infinite Scale.|

|Having constructed your Hadean Pillar of Infinity and achieved Absolute Infinity, this demarcation focuses on the full comprehension and actualization of THE Infinite Cause that defines your existence. The chain of your Cause runs from your birth through your Infinity through the Seed of Observable Existence. This chain must be understood completely.|

|Your Hadean Pillar of Infinity must be saturated with the authority of your Cause. Every Civilization actualized within it must resonate with the fundamental truth of your emergence. The Pillar becomes not merely a structure of power but a monument to THE Infinite Cause itself.|

|Upon completing Infinitas Causa, you will stand at the peak of THE First Infinite Scale.|

|However, transition to THE Second Infinite Scale requires one final advancement.|

|Transcendent Infinity.|

|This level of Infinity lies beyond Absolute Infinity and can only potentially be attained during the transition itself. Transcendent Infinity represents Infinity that has become indistinguishable from Causality.|

|This advancement cannot be achieved while remaining at THE First Infinite Scale. It is the bridge between Scales, the transformation that marks the difference between standing at the peak and stepping beyond it.|

|I should note that this ninth iteration represents significant refinement over previous versions. Earlier designs attempted to incorporate too many separate structures, creating frameworks that would have been powerful but fragmented. This version maintains elegance through unity. One Pillar. Unlimited Civilizations. Infinity as the foundation for everything.|

...!

Chapter 5118: THE First Infinite Scale! III

He wanted to design his First Scale to be straightforward, intuitive, and unique but not overly complex.

So everything he had done up to this point, all the transformations and integrations and impossible advancements, he neatly put a bow on it and called it Infinitas Corpus, The Infinite Body. He had achieved the apex of this stage. Or at least it was what most would consider to be the apex of THE First Scale.

Even though he could use its power to fight against entities at THE Second Scale of Vakochevs Scales of Existence.

And when he advanced from Infinitas Corpus, he would only be on the second level of his own Scale of Existence. He couldnt quite say exactly where his power would be after that advancement, couldnt predict what completing Infinitas Architectura would mean in practical terms. THE Deliverance would be a good and fearsome enemy to test things out against when the time came.

But right now, since he had the outline, he would begin implementing it.

When designing his own Scale, he didnt want it to be something as convoluted as what others in the old worlds and realms he had passed through theorized about systems of power. Nothing as crazy as building his Scales with stages like Void Refining, Body Integration, Mahayana, and some kind of Tribulation!

No.

That was too much!

Infinitas Corpus, Infinitas Architectura, Infinitas Causa.

Three demarcations. One Pillar. Unlimited potential.

And right now...

"I have been stuck on this level for too long."

Noahs voice emerged with conviction that pressed against the surrounding environment.

"Has it already been a day? A few days? Far too long!"

His eyes blazed brighter as he rose from his seated position.

"I shall advance toward Infinitas Architectura where Absolute Infinity awaits."

HUUM!

...!

The island he occupied began to tremble beneath forces that transcended physical causation.

He rose from the grassland and floated upward, his body lifting through air that grew thicker with authority as he ascended. He rose to the midpoint of this realm, that space where the endless blue sea below mirrored the endless blue sea above. Two oceans stretching infinitely in opposite directions, and he floated between them like a singular point of purpose suspended in aquatic infinity.

His eyes were unfathomably bright as he considered what he was about to attempt.

So far, it was just ideas. Even though they were ideas he had refined through nine iterations of careful design, nobody had told Noah they would work. They might succeed brilliantly. They might fail catastrophically. There was no precedent for what he was doing because no one had ever done it before.

He was a Pioneer.

He was carving this path himself, and if he went wrong anywhere, it would be very costly. There were no teachers to correct his mistakes, no ancient texts describing how to construct a Hadean Pillar of Infinity, no accumulated wisdom from countless practitioners who had walked this road before him.

There was only him.

So...

"Infinitas Architectura."

He called out the name as his body began generating even more endless Quintessence Infiniforce. Blue Infinity gathered all around him in concentrations that would have driven most beings to madness. Observable Force formed into golden rivers that circled his position.

The construction of a singular internal structure that would serve as the foundation for everything that followed.

He would build a Hadean Pillar of Infinity within his existence.

Rather than constructing multiple separate pillars for different authorities, he would create a single Pillar that could be built up by as many Civilizations as he could actualize within it. Each Civilization he congealed into stable form would become another layer of the Hadean Pillar of Infinity, another foundation stone supporting the structure he was building.

Observable Force would be the binding agent holding these actualized Civilizations together. Quintessence Infiniforce would serve as the animating principle allowing them to function as a unified whole rather than separate fragments.

He made sure he understood everything well.

Then he took a step.

The motion seemed mundane. One foot lifting, moving forward through space, descending toward a surface that existed only in concept rather than physical reality. It was a step that anyone could take, a movement so basic that infants learned it within their first year of life.

But with this step, this entire realm became bathed in blue and gold and multicolored brilliance.

Infinite seas surged into that single motion. Every drop of Observable Force he had access to, every mote of Quintessence Infiniforce his existence generated, every trace of authority he could muster flowed into the act of bringing his foot down.

When it landed, something within him shattered.

BOOM!

A barrier he hadnt known existed broke apart, and what emerged from behind it defied description.

A single massive Pillar rose up from within his existence.

It stretched out in this realm first, its base forming somewhere in the depths of his Hadean Organ of Civilization before expanding outward in all directions. The Pillar passed through this Oceanus-like domain without disturbing the twin seas above and below, its form somehow existing alongside physical reality rather than displacing it.

Then it stretched further.

Past other thousands of realms across THE Infiniverse, the Pillar extended. Through territories that held sacred herbs and tumultuous seas and floating landmasses of every description. THE Infiniverse trembled as this construct rose through her depths, her humanoid manifestation opening her eyes with surprise as something vast moved through her very being.

The Pillar rose out of THE Infiniverse entirely.

It emerged into THE Wastes. The multicolored rain of THE Pluvial Epoch fell upon its surface as it continued stretching upward, higher and higher, showing no signs of stopping.

Infinitely.

The Pillar was grand beyond comprehension, its surface blazing with multicolored light that shifted through every hue existence had ever named. Golden bands wrapped around its circumference at irregular intervals, patterns of Observable Force that served as binding agents even as they contributed to its beauty.

But for all its grandeur, the Pillar was hollow.

Its interior waited to be filled. The Civilizations that would form its layers had not yet been actualized. The structure existed, but its contents remained potential rather than actual. It was a monument waiting for meaning, a foundation waiting for what would be built upon it.

The Pillar crossed THE Wastes and continued rising.

It flashed momentarily in different Primordial Realms, its illusory form manifesting wherever existence permitted its passage. Beings across countless territories looked up as something impossible bloomed across their skies, a Pillar that seemed to connect the lowest depths to the highest heights while belonging to neither!

It even manifested across Prima Indifferentia.

That region of Undivided Ones and Formless Terrors and Primordial Architects witnessed the Pillars passage through their domain, ancient consciousnesses stirring with confusion at something they couldnt categorize. The white gold sea that defined their home rippled with disturbance that had nothing to do with current or tide.

On this day, across Observable Existence, an Infinite Pillar bloomed momentarily!

Many witnessed it!

And they wondered.

What the fuck is that?!

---

THE Wyld stretched endlessly in ways that defied sanity.

This region existed as the true home of Primordial Architects, but "home" implied comfort that THE Wyld did not provide. It was a realm of primal power and ancient danger, where the line between hunter and hunted shifted with each passing moment. Survival here required strength that most beings couldnt comprehend.

THE Creature stood within a forest that looked like something from primeval times.

Trees rose hundreds of meters high, their bark cracite with age of THE First Cause. Branches intertwined overhead in canopies so thick that whatever passed for sky in THE Wyld remained invisible. Bioluminescent fungi clung to trunks and roots, providing illumination that painted everything in shades of ethereal green and deep violet.

Abundant existential energy saturated every molecule of this forest.

Just breathing here would have advanced most First Scale beings through multiple stages of cultivation. The concentration of authority pressed against everything with density that made the richest regions of normal Observable Existence seem impoverished by comparison. This was why Primordial Architects thrived in THE Wyld despite its dangers. The rewards matched the risks.

Milky gold rivers of light and blood flowed around the small clearing where THE Creature stood.

The liquid wasnt water. It was something between Observable Force and vital fluid, the runoff from conflicts that had occurred in this location recently. Very recently!

The blood was still warm, still carrying traces of authority from beings who had been alive mere minutes ago.

Seven Primordial Architects lay scattered around the clearing.

Their bodies were arranged in positions that spoke of desperate combat and sudden defeat. Some had fallen while trying to flee. Others had died mid-attack, their offensive postures frozen by death before they could complete their strikes. Three bore Rhyacian Tier classifications based on their residual authority. Four had been Calymmian.

All of them were dead now!

Anaximander stood near the edge of the clearing with his arms crossed at all this violence.

Tairiyya floated nearby. She said nothing, but her attention remained fixed on their leader.

THE Creature himself knelt beside one of the fallen Calymmian entities.

His hands were buried wrist-deep in the corpses chest cavity, having torn through Proterozoic Bones and flesh to reach what lay beneath. Blood coated his arms up to the elbows, thick and dark and still carrying warmth from the life it had recently supported. His expression held nothing but focus as he worked.

He pulled out a heart.

The organ was massive, and it pulsed with residual authority despite its owners death. Proterozoic classification had transformed it into something far beyond mere muscle and blood vessels. It was a repository of power, a concentrated source of everything its original owner had cultivated across eons of existence!

THE Creature brought it to his mouth and bit! He chewed slowly and deliberately, savoring the authority that flooded into his existence with each swallow.

When he finished the heart, he reached back into the corpse for other organs.

Lungs came next, their Proterozoic structure providing different flavors of authority than the heart had offered. Then the liver. Then the kidneys. Each organ consumed added to what THE Creature was becoming, each bite pushing him further along whatever path he had chosen when he burned away his Primordial Architect classification!

It was during this brutal feast that the sky above THE Wyld changed.

THE Creature raised his head, blood dripping from his chin as his eyes fixed on something that hadnt been there moments before.

An illusory Pillar stretched across the sky!

Multicolored and banded with gold, it rose from somewhere far below and extended toward heights that even THE Wylds strange geometry couldnt contain. The Pillar blazed with power that pressed against everything nearby!

Anaximander looked up at the same moment, his eyes widening with surprise.

"What... is that?"

THE Creature studied the Pillar for several long seconds as if he could see things others couldnt.

Blood continued dripping from his chin as a smile spread across his features.

"It burns with Infinity."

He looked at Anaximander with eyes that held fire from a recently used THE Silurian Light.

"So it may just be the one you continue to worry about that I tell you not to worry about."

...!

Anaximander blinked at this assessment, his surprise deepening as he looked back toward the Pillar still blazing across the sky.

THE Creature returned his attention to the corpse before him, reaching for another organ as he continued.

"When pushed, when bullied, when adversity presses down and down without mercy or pause..."

He tore out what might have been a Proterozoic spleen and examined it with clinical interest.

"It can awaken a bloody beast within. And that bloody beast may become its own adversity for those who thought themselves the predators."

His smile grew sharper.

He bit into the spleen, chewing thoughtfully.

"Adversity breeds greatness. I still wait to see if Erwin will bloom into something astounding from my pressure..."

...!

THE Creature returned to his eating with renewed focus, the Pillar above beginning to fade as whatever power had manifested it settled back into its source. The illusory structure grew translucent, then ghostly, then disappeared entirely as if it had never been there at all.

But everyone who had seen it would remember.

Everyone who had witnessed it would wonder!

Anaximander threw his head back and laughed.

The sound rang out across the primeval forest with joy that seemed inappropriate given the corpses surrounding them, but it was genuine!

Chapter 5119: THE First Infinite Scale! IV

As he looked at the Pillar that stretched out endlessly, Noah felt something fundamental shift within his existence.

It was as if he had opened floodgates he hadnt known were closed. The concentration of Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force within him, which had seemed almost full mere moments ago, now felt like it could expand countless more times. His capacity hadnt merely increased. The very concept of capacity had changed, transforming from a finite container into something that could grow without boundary!

This was what he had been missing.

This was what standing at the supposed peak of THE First Scale had denied him. A ceiling he couldnt perceive had been pressing down on his potential, limiting what he could hold and channel and become. Now that ceiling was gone, shattered by the construction of something that had never existed before.

This was Infinitas Architectura!

But not really. Not yet!

Because he hadnt begun building.

The Hadean Pillar of Infinity held infinite potential, but it was currently hollow. A grand structure with no contents. A monument to what could be rather than what was. Its multicolored surface blazed with authority that came from its nature rather than its substance, potential rather than actualization.

Noah waved his hand.

The Pillars endless nature, which had stretched across all of Observable Existence moments before, began to fade.

What remained was a Pillar the height of this Oceanus-like realm he occupied, its form contained within THE Infiniverse rather than bleeding across everything that existed.

He looked down.

On the island far below, between the twin seas that stretched above and beneath, Naldine was looking up with a stern expression. Her singularity-dotted eyes studied the Pillar with attention that held something between analysis and wariness. She was trying to gauge his power, trying to understand what she had just witnessed!

Let her wonder.

Inside that blinding hollow Pillar of Infinity, Noah floated toward its base.

The interior was vast beyond comprehension, space that somehow existed within his existence while also occupying physical territory in the realm around him. The walls curved away in every direction, multicolored surfaces that awaited the Civilizations he would actualize upon them. But the floor was where everything would begin. The foundation upon which all else would be built.

"At the base of all of it will be Mana."

His voice emerged with conviction that pressed against the hollow interior.

"THE First Tongue."

HUUM!

The base of this glorious Pillar would have nothing except the one thing he had always possessed. The one constant across every transformation, every advancement, every impossible achievement.

THE First Tongue had been his Civilization before he knew what Civilizations were.

It would be his foundation now.

Noah knelt down at the base of his Pillar.

From his hands, endless blue light permeated outward. It wasnt mere illumination but something far more fundamental, the very essence of what THE First Tongue represented made visible through his intention. Infinite absolute Seals began manifesting around him, weavings of authority that represented the twenty-seven Phonemes that comprised the foundational language of existence.

They gushed out endlessly, these Seals, as if they were seeds being planted on the very base of this Pillar of Infinity.

The twenty-seven letters formed into Logos. Into words. They mixed into each other countless times, creating variations and combinations that multiplied beyond what simple mathematics could describe. Each Phoneme touched each other Phoneme, creating new meanings. Those meanings combined with other meanings, creating concepts. Philologies and Archai bloomed!

Those concepts intertwined with other concepts, creating authorities.

As if the seeds were blooming, the entire basal region of the Pillar began to transform.

Illusory blue seeds sprouted from the floor. They pushed upward through nothing, through potential space that hadnt existed until they needed it to exist. Saplings emerged from those seeds, their forms crystalline and luminous, their branches reaching toward the hollow heights above. The saplings flourished into trees, their growth accelerating past what any natural process could achieve.

A forest of THE First Tongue rose around Noah.

The color blue began rising in concentration all around him. It climbed past his knees, his waist, his chest. It exceeded his height and continued climbing, the forest growing denser and grander with each passing moment. Trees of language stretched toward the Pillars interior heights, their branches heavy with words that hadnt been spoken yet, their leaves inscribed with meanings that most beings couldnt comprehend.

At the very peak of all of it, something began to form.

A radiant Grimoire of Hadean Lexicons bloomed into existence.

The book was massive, its cover blazing with multicolored light that declared its nature without need for explanation. Its pages fluttered endlessly, never settling on a single configuration, each flutter revealing new words and new meanings and new possibilities. It was the actualization of THE First Tongue.

The moment this occurred, everything changed.

Rivers of golden Observable Force surged into this basal floor from somewhere beyond the Pillars walls. Observable Force rushed toward the actualized Civilization with purpose that felt almost desperate. It permeated across everything, across every tree and every branch and every leaf and every word.

The Pillar of Infinity began to shine unfathomably bright.

|THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity has been established.|

Ruinations voice emerged with wonder!

|The first Civilization has been actualized within its structure. THE First Tongue now exists as a permanent foundation. Its power flows through your Pillar continuously, contributing to everything built upon it.|

|You have officially stepped onto Infinitas Architectura, The Infinite Architecture, of THE First Infinite Scale of Existence.|

|Your methodology has officially begun pioneering something new.|

|You deviate from Vakochevs Scales of Existence.|

...!

The words were grand ones.

Noahs body inside his Pillar of Infinity radiated blinding light of brilliance that pressed against the crystalline forest surrounding him. His eyes shot out multicolored pillars of light that reached toward the Grimoire floating at the peak of his actualized foundation. Every aspect of his existence resonated with what he had just achieved.

Officially on his own path!

Deviating from Vakochevs Scales of Existence!

At this point...

|Error.|

HUUM!

Ruinations voice buzzed with caution that hadnt been present moments before.

|New weavings of information from a foreign source incoming. Unable to stop them.|

...!

Noahs eyes became sharp as he sensed something pressing against his consciousness from outside.

Momentarily, Ruinations voice and prompts faded. Her presence retreated as if pushed aside by something that possessed authority she couldnt contest. In front of his eyes, in blue-bordered boxes and radiant blue letters that differed from Ruinations golden notifications, new prompts bloomed.

A voice accompanied them.

It felt deep and ancient and heavy, carrying the weight of someone who had observed existence across spans that made eons seem like heartbeats. It wasnt threatening. It wasnt aggressive!

It simply was, the way mountains simply were, the way oceans simply were!

|...The path you have taken is an arduous and difficult one.|

The voice pressed against his consciousness with intensity!

|But it is welcomed.|

A pause that felt like centuries compressed into moments.

|The only thing I can tell you is to Persevere. Everything will stand in your way, but Persevere. Existence itself will oppose you, but Persevere. Enemies will seek your destruction, but Persevere. Allies will doubt your methods, but Persevere. Even family may stand in your way, questioning whether your path leads anywhere worth reaching.|

The voice grew heavier.

|Still, Persevere.|

Another pause.

|Osmont, right? Against all odds, against every force that will try to crush what you are building, against the weight of how things have always been...|

The ancient voice carried something that might have been respect.

|I, Vakochev, can only advise you to Persevere. And just maybe, if you succeed, I will see you in that place.|

The final word emerged with weight that shook his existence to its foundations.

|PERSEVERE!|

BOOM!

When that deep and ancient voice finished, Noah found his brows covered with sweat that shouldnt have been possible for a Hadean Lifeform to produce!

His eyes shone fiercely as he processed what had just occurred. His nose breathed out flames of Infinity that scorched the crystalline trees nearest to him.

He...fully felt it now.

He had lost any connection he had with Vakochevs Scales of Existence.

The framework that had governed power across Existence since before most current beings were born no longer applied to him. He couldnt be measured by its standards because he had chosen to reject those standards entirely. The Scales that told everyone else where they stood and how far they had to go would tell him nothing.

He was very much alone.

A Pioneer, on his own!

Chapter 5120: Advancement! I

It is lonely at the top.

Such words have been uttered across countless civilizations and eons, spoken by beings who climbed higher than their peers and found themselves standing alone in territories no one else could reach!

But the loneliness of achievement pales in comparison to the loneliness of pioneering.

Those who reach the top of established paths at least have the comfort of knowing others have stood where they stand. They can look down and see the trail that led them upward, they can identify the footprints of predecessors who validated their journey through completion. They are alone in position but not in experience.

Pioneers have no such comfort.

They walk paths that do not exist until their feet touch ground. They climb mountains that have no peaks until they declare a stopping point. Every step is a question without a guaranteed answer, every advancement a gamble that could end in triumph or catastrophe with equal probability.

Who else can share their vision? By definition, no one!

No one!

If others could see what they see, the path would already exist. The Pioneers curse is to perceive possibilities that remain invisible to everyone else, to feel compelled toward destinations that others cannot even imagine. They speak of what theyre building and receive blank stares in return, confusion from those who cannot comprehend why anyone would abandon the safety of established routes.

And when Pioneers succeed, when they carve paths that others will eventually follow, those who come after will never understand what was required. They will walk the completed road and see only the road. They will not see the false starts, the collapsed tunnels, the chasms that nearly swallowed the one who built this passage. They will not know how many times the Pioneer considered turning back, how many moments of despair preceded each breakthrough, how much blood and sweat and tears soaked into foundations that now appear solid and inevitable.

The path will seem obvious in retrospect.

"Of course this was possible," they will say. "Of course someone would eventually do this."

But the Pioneer knew nothing was obvious. The Pioneer knew that "eventually" almost became "never" countless times during the construction. The Pioneer carries scars that the paths future travelers will never see and could never appreciate!

This is the price of going first.

This...is what it means to be alone.

Noah felt a sense of emptiness settle into his existence.

It wasnt pain or fear, just absence. He had belonged to some structure he couldnt perceive before, some framework that had given him meaning and definition without his awareness. Vakochevs Scales had been there like gravity, invisible but constant, telling him where he stood in relation to everything else. Now that definition was gone.

He could fall or stumble at any moment. There were no more markers telling him which direction was up. There was no more system declaring whether his next step would be advancement or regression. He floated in conceptual void where measurement itself had ceased to apply.

But in this lost sensation, he felt something else!

A glimmer of Infinity rising within him.

HUUM!

Infinity helped him up. Infinity kept him stable. The very foundation he had chosen to build upon refused to let him collapse into the emptiness that threatened to swallow him. It pressed against the void with authority that declared emptiness was just another form of potential, and potential was something Infinity understood intimately.

Because even though he did not have Vakochevs Scales of Existence anymore, he was now forging his Infinite Scales of Existence!

His own framework. His own definitions. His own meaning!

HUUM!

Noah rose up sternly within his Hadean Pillar of Infinity.

He floated above the level where THE First Tongue had been actualized, past the crystalline forest of blue trees and the Grimoire of Hadean Lexicons that crowned its peaks. The foundation was complete. Now came the construction that would fill this hollow monument with substance worthy of its potential.

He looked upward toward the vast empty space that awaited the next Civilization.

"Existence."

His voice emerged calm and measured.

Below him, the actualized First Tongue responded to his call.

Blue Mana began flowing upward from the forest of language like endless water rising against gravity. It climbed through the Pillars interior in streams that wove around each other, rivers of THE First Tongue ascending toward the level where Noah floated. The blue light was beautiful in its purity, carrying the foundational authority of the language that underpinned all of reality.

Then it began to transform.

The blue started bubbling as if heated by invisible flames. Colors emerged from within the azure streams, reds and golds and greens and violets bleeding outward from cores that had been uniform moments before. The Mana was being elevated, THE First Tongue serving as the base material from which something grander would be forged.

The Civilization of Existence manifested as endlessly rising multicolored flames.

They didnt burn the way normal fire burned. They declared that things were rather than were not. The flames rose in columns and curtains and spiraling towers, their heat carrying the warmth of reality itself pressing against the void of non-being. It looked like a forge! A cosmic forge where existence itself was hammered into shape from raw potential.

When the actualization completed, the second level of his Pillar blazed with authority that made THE First Tongue seem gentle by comparison.

Noah floated within those multicolored flames without discomfort.

"Existence...is not separate from Infinity," he said, his tone thoughtful and precise. "Infinity makes Existence possible by providing the endless potential from which reality emerges. And Existence gives Infinity meaning by actualizing that potential into something that matters. They need each other. One without the other is incomplete."

He paused, watching the flames dance around him.

"This is why they belong in the same Pillar. They are not separate foundations competing for primacy, they are aspects of the same fundamental truth. The Oldest Paradox understood this. I understand it now."

HUUM!

The flames of Existence settled into stable weavings as Observable Force and Infinity surged through them, golden rivers binding this second Civilization to the first. The Pillar grew brighter, its hollow interior now holding two levels of actualized authority stacked upon each other.

Noah rose higher.

He passed through the multicolored flames of Existence, their heat parting around him like water around a stone. Above them, more empty space awaited. More potential crying out for actualization! More levels to be built before his Pillar would approach anything resembling completion.

"Paradox."

The word emerged with the same deliberation he had used before.

Below, THE First Tongue and Existence responded together.

Blue Mana rose from the forest of language, climbing through the flames of Existence and absorbing their multicolored authority as it passed. The streams that emerged above the second level held both the foundational nature of THE First Tongue and the creative heat of Existence, combined into something that vibrated with tension between contradictory states.

The transformation began differently this time.

Rather than bubbling into new colors, the ascending streams started splitting. Each river of combined authority divided into two rivers flowing in opposite directions while somehow remaining in the same space. They contradicted themselves visually, logically, fundamentally. They were and were not. They moved and remained still. They existed in multiple states simultaneously because Paradox refused to accept that only one state could be true.

The Civilization of Paradox manifested as infinite reflections facing each other.

Mirrors made of crystallized contradiction stretched across this level of the Pillar, each one showing images that shouldnt have been possible. Noah saw himself in one mirror as a human throwing fireballs. In another, as THE Youngest standing before a shadowy THE Deliverance. In a third, as something he hadnt become yet, forms that existed only in potential futures that may or may not arrive. All of them were him. None of them were him. The Paradox refused to resolve!

Oh!

"Paradox...is Infinitys closest sibling," Noah observed, his voice steady despite the impossible reflections surrounding him. "Both reject limitation. Both insist that boundaries are suggestions rather than laws. The difference is that Infinity achieves the impossible by having no end, while Paradox achieves it by holding contradictions together until they stop being contradictions."

He looked at a mirror showing himself failing, then at one showing himself succeeding.

"Ive learned to appreciate Paradox. It taught me that being weak and strong simultaneously is...a grand strategy."

HUUM!

Chapter 5121: Advancement! II

The mirrors of Paradox settled, their contradictions stabilizing into patterns that shouldnt have been stable. Infinity and Observable Force flowed through them, blue and golden binding agents connecting this third level to everything below. The Pillar blazed brighter still.

Noah rose again.

Three levels complete. One more to go before the foundation of his Hadean Pillar of Infinity would hold all four Aspects of THE Oldest Paradox in Existence!

"Chaos."

The final word fell into the Pillars interior with weight that belied its simple pronunciation.

Everything below responded.

Blue Mana from THE First Tongue. Multicolored flames from Existence. Contradictory reflections from Paradox. All of it rose together, streams and fires and mirrors ascending in combinations that grew more unstable with each passing moment. The authority climbing toward this final level held everything that had come before, all the foundational aspects combining into something that threatened to tear itself apart at any moment.

That was the point.

The transformation was violent!

Chaotic!

The ascending authority didnt bubble or split. It exploded. It collapsed. It reformed in configurations that lasted milliseconds before shattering into new configurations equally temporary. Nothing held. Nothing stabilized. Nothing accepted the concept of permanence because Chaos refused to acknowledge that anything should remain the same for longer than it chose to.

The Civilization of Chaos manifested as an eternal storm.

Lightning made of pure possibility arced between clouds made of dissolved certainty. Winds carrying fragments of reality that had been torn apart howled through this level of the Pillar without pattern or purpose. Everything was destruction. Everything was creation!

The distinction between the two ceased to exist because Chaos saw no difference between breaking and building.

Noah stood at the center of the storm, his Hadean body untouched by devastation that would have erased lesser beings.

"Chaos is what Infinity looks like when you remove all the rules." His voice cut through the howling winds with calm that seemed inappropriate. "Pure potential without direction.
